html:
The Havasupai are a Native American people who have lived in and around the Grand Canyon in Arizona for at least 800 years. Their name means "people of the blue-green water", after Havasu Creek, a side stream of the Colorado River.

They speak a Yuman language, close to that of their neighbours the Hualapai. For centuries they farmed maize, beans and squash on the canyon floor in summer and moved up to the plateau in winter to hunt and gather. They traded with the Hopi to the east.

Their lands once covered about 6,500 square kilometres. In 1882 the United States confined them to a reservation of a few hundred hectares in the canyon. In 1975 Congress returned some 75,000 hectares of plateau land to them. Their village, Supai, can still be reached only on foot, by horse or by helicopter. See also Havasu Baaja on the modern map.
